messages:
mia: Quick pass on a small dark-mode tweak — proposing a "moonlit grid" swatch to improve chart gridlines and panel separation without making syntax text wash out. Low-risk change: keep base surfaces same, add mid-toned grid + warmer highlight for token heatmap. Thoughts?

dan: Can you paste the hexes so I can run visual diffs across dashboards?

mia: Sure — pasted below (quick notes after):
```
--moonlit-bg: #0b0f12  /* console background */
--moonlit-surface: #0f1417  /* panels */
--grid-accent: #3f5b73  /* subtle grid / separators */
--accent-strong: #69b6ff  /* primary highlight, e.g., selected route */
--accent-muted: #2c3f4a  /* button hover / muted badges */
--heat-low: #2b3034  /* token heat baseline */
--heat-mid: #3f6a55  /* mid heat (greenish) */
--heat-high: #ffcc6a /* high heat (warm) */
--syntax-keyword: #95c9ff
--syntax-string: #cfe89b
--axis-label: #9fb0b6
```

ashley: First glance: the grid-accent on moonlit-surface looks fine, but accent-strong (#69b6ff) on bg (#0b0f12) might be ~3.9:1 contrast. WCAG AA for large text is 3:1 but normal text needs 4.5:1 — so interactive text/icons could fail.

kevin: Also flagging colorblindness: the greenish mid heat + warm high could be ambiguous for deuteranopia if used together on same scale. We should prefer a single-hue luminance ramp or use a colorblind-friendly diverging map.

mia: Good catches. My intent was to keep the heatmap bivariate (cool-mid-warm) for at-a-glance, but happy to switch to single-hue ramp for accessibility. Options: desaturate accent-strong to get contrast, and change heatmap to single-hue warm ramp (dark -> amber).

dan: Quick utility I used to test: `d3.scaleSequential(d3.interpolateOrRd).domain([0,1])` — gives an OrRd single-hue ramp that reads by luminance. Also ran a11y sim locally.

ashley: If we go single-hue, prefer a perceptually-uniform ramp (Viridis or OrRd) so relative differences are clear. Also axis labels look low-contrast on small charts — axis-label (#9fb0b6) on surface (#0f1417) is ~4.3:1, borderline for small text. Recommend bump to #b7c6cb.

mia: Fine by me. Proposed adjustments:
```
--accent-strong: #5ea7e8  /* slightly darker for contrast */
--heat-low: #191d1f
--heat-mid: #3a2b12
--heat-high: #ffbf5a  /* OrRd-ish final */
--axis-label: #b7c6cb
```

dan: I pushed a quick branch with the CSS vars and a screenshot to the design branch: https://git.company/repo/branches/moonlit-grid (please review). I also added a script to generate palette previews.

kevin: I'll run the normal+deuteranopia/protanopia simulations on that branch. Quick note: avoid using both blue accent + amber highlights for critical status — they can read as the same weight in some sims. Suggest making critical states use saturated red/orange with distinct icon shape.

ashley: Copy nits — for the chart legend label we had "Token density" which is vague. Suggest "Token heat (requests/min)" or just "Token density (rps)" depending on context. Also confirm tooltip copy is truncated-friendly.

mia: Agree: "Token heat (rps)". I'll update copy on the branch. Also will add a short accessibility checklist to the PR description: contrast ratios, colorblind sim results, keyboard focus style check.

design-bot: Contrast scan results (from branch):
- accent-strong (#5ea7e8) on bg (#0b0f12): 4.5:1 PASS for normal UI elements.
- axis-label (#b7c6cb) on surface (#0f1417): 5.0:1 PASS for small text.
- heatmap palette (OrRd ramp) simulated for deuteranopia: preserves luminance ordering PASS.

mia: Awesome — thanks bot. Next steps:
- dan: finalize vars + push final screenshots to branch (assigned)
- ashley: formal a11y pass + update PR checklist (assigned)
- kevin: colorblind sims + confirm icon shapes for critical (assigned)
- mia: update legends/copy and sign off visuals (assigned)

kevin: I'll post results by EOD with snapshots. If any of the sims fail we'll try a lightness-only ramp (gray->amber) as fallback.

dan: Merged interim styles to `staging-theme` so the dashboard preview shows changes. Will revert if anything breaks.

mia: Thanks all — keeping this scoped small so we can ship the grid + heatmap change in next minor release. :thumbsup:
